context_switch.note: One of the three that touch no Lua. Two changes moved it in opposite directions and the net is what matters: 9.812 -> 6.875 when the FP register file stopped being saved on every switch, then 6.875 -> 8.375 when round robin became a priority queue. Net -14.6% against the eager-FP round-robin number, with priorities and preemption-on-wake gained. The +21.8% half is the cost of indexing eight queues and maintaining an occupancy mask instead of following one head pointer; the obvious version, which scanned the levels, cost twice that and the benchmark caught it the same day.
context_switch.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

exception.note: The cost of taking and returning from a synchronous exception. 7.250 -> 7.562, +4.3%, and it is the price of lazy FP save rather than a regression to chase: every exception now begins by asking whether it is an FP trap, because that question has to be answered before anything else looks at the frame. One comparison, paid on every exception, to save the whole register file on every context switch - `context_switch` went down 29.9% and `ipc_roundtrip` 16.2% in the same change.
exception.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

gc_pause_max.note: The worst single collector step, measured in a process. 78221, drifting up with what the process carries in the same way serialize does and by far less: 78129 before gfx, 78199 after, 78221 with the font. A long step is dominated by the 3000-object heap the benchmark builds rather than by a handful of library tables. Before that it was 77860, running inside the kernel with interrupts masked. Leaving EL1 cost the interpreter +0.3% and nothing else: a collector step costs the same at either privilege level. Interrupts are live in the window now, because a process cannot mask them, and for a pause metric that is more honest rather than less - a pause the user feels includes the tick that landed in it.
gc_pause_max.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

ipc_roundtrip.note: A minimal message: the floor of the IPC path, including the capability lookup. 36.251 -> 30.376 from lazy FP save, then back to 36.438 with the priority scheduler - a round trip is two switches, so it pays the policy twice. Net flat against two days earlier, which is the honest way to read it: lazy FP bought the priority queue rather than the priority queue being free. What was gained for it is a bounded wait for a higher-priority thread, which this benchmark cannot see.
ipc_roundtrip.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0

serialize.note: Best of five processes within a run. **This benchmark is sensitive to what else is in the process**, not only to the serialiser: every library the image opens is more objects for the collector to pace against. 1450.574 -> 1498.325, +3.3%, when the PDF scanner and the inflate kit joined the user image; `serialize.c` was untouched. If it moves and nothing in `serialize.c` or `sys_user.c` did, look at what was added. Making it independent of its process - a fixed GC pause and a forced collection before the loop - is a known improvement and is still not done.
serialize.unit: counter ticks per operation, QEMU -icount shift=0
